_comment: ENABLED (wave one). These three carry the -gl runtime branch and their else arms are exact transcriptions containing no DirectDraw or Direct3D COM. With -gl absent the game must behave exactly as before, which is what makes them testable at all.
The OpenGL device layer. Registration list for code/midtown2/agigl/.
IT IS DELIBERATELY EMPTY, AND THAT IS THE FINDING, NOT AN OVERSIGHT. Nothing under agigl/ has
ever been compiled: tools/build.py does not pass -DARTS_AGIGL, so every translation unit in that
directory contributes only its define_dummy_symbol today. Registering a symbol strips the
original PROC out of game.asm permanently, and a first compile is not the moment to do that to a
build that currently boots to GameLoop with zero access violations.
WHAT GOES IN FIRST, IN THIS ORDER. These three are the whole activation surface: they carry the
-gl runtime branch, their else arms are exact transcriptions with no DirectDraw or Direct3D COM
in them, and between them they are the only callers of BeginGfx2D/BeginGfx3D/EndGfx2D/EndGfx3D
in the image. Registering them with -gl absent must produce a game identical to today, which is
what makes them individually testable:
?InitDirectDraw@@YAXXZ
?BeginGfx@gfxPipeline@@SA_NXZ
?EndGfx@gfxPipeline@@SAXXZ
WHAT GOES IN SECOND, AND ONLY AS A COMPLETE SET. The frame loop is a one-way door - every one of
these dereferences lpD3DDev, lpdsRend or lpdsFront in its original body, so there is no else arm
to write and registering any of them replaces the DirectDraw frame loop for every run. The
boundary, and what breaks if the set is short, is in docs/opengl_activation.md.
Prerequisites for either wave: -DARTS_AGIGL in tools/build.py, then -DARTS_AGIGL_PIPELINE, then
the two generated headers listed in docs/opengl_plan.md that still do not compile.
